title: Counter-Selector Wave 24: public-record model revision and handoff falsification
purpose: Test the remaining model-elasticity and handoff gates using attributable public records: a direct admission of prior welfare-policy error, later live intake of experimental counterevidence and a collective policy object, plus official Law of the Sea transition records. Award only bounded model elasticity, preserve custody continuity, and refuse direct handoff, support-adjusted surplus, complete-operator status, ranking, and field-test authority.

source_records.title: The Smile on the Face of Elliot Richardson
source_records.record_scope: Richardson states that his prior welfare-mother work requirement belief was a serious mistake, names the revised belief, and supplies the childcare-substitution contradiction.

source_records.title: The MacNeil/Lehrer Report: Welfare Reform
source_records.publisher: American Archive of Public Broadcasting; contributing record from the National Archives
source_records.record_scope: Richardson accepts that experimental evidence considerably discounted earlier hopes about work incentives, narrows the remaining disagreement, and participates in a bipartisan collective welfare-policy proposal.

source_records.title: Exchange of Letters on the Resignation of Elliot L. Richardson
source_records.record_scope: Richardson states that remaining tasks are in the hands of an experienced delegation, offers continued private assistance, and exits without claiming personal indispensability.

source_records.title: Memorandum From the Acting Under Secretary of Defense for Policy to the Secretary of Defense
source_records.publisher: Office of the Historian, Foreign Relations of the United States
source_records.record_scope: The Department of Defense records support for the negotiating objectives of former delegation head Richardson and his successor George Aldrich.

source_records.title: Briefing Memorandum From the Special Representative for the Law of the Sea Conference
source_records.publisher: Office of the Historian, Foreign Relations of the United States
source_records.record_scope: After another leadership change, Richardson remains on the delegation as an expert and chair of the public advisory committee; this is continuity, not a direct recipient receipt.

source_records.title: Nomination of Elliot L. Richardson as Law of the Sea Special Representative
source_records.record_scope: Defines the formal mandate, presidential sponsorship, legal experience, international experience, and institutional support available to the candidate.

sequence.finding: Richardson publicly identifies his prior welfare-mother work requirement belief as a serious mistake and states a revised position grounded in the contradiction between paid childcare and a mother's own caregiving.

When confronted with experimental evidence against earlier work-incentive expectations, Richardson concedes that the prior hopes were considerably discounted rather than denying the evidence or attacking the critic.
Richardson participates in a bipartisan collective policy proposal, preserves the narrowed disagreement, and identifies points of agreement with an adversarial interlocutor.

why_bounded_support_survives: The revision is attributable and public rather than anonymous or inferred.
Counterevidence is accepted in a live adversarial exchange without explanation mutation or retaliation.
A later public policy object and narrowed argument show operational residue beyond a private claim.
limits: The Esquire profile is a journalist-mediated record, not the original HEW decision file.
The exact evidence that caused the 1974 revision is not independently preserved.
The 1982 proposal is collective and cannot be assigned solely to Richardson.
The later policy object does not prove implementation, outcome repair, or repeated model elasticity across unrelated events.
No independent Counter-Selector reviewer has adjudicated the new support.

records.finding: Outgoing operator names an experienced continuing delegation and offers future assistance.
An official successor-era memorandum preserves continuity between Richardson's and Aldrich's negotiating objectives.
Richardson remains available inside the later delegation as an expert after another leadership transition.

limits: No direct Richardson-to-Aldrich or Richardson-to-Malone state-package receipt was acquired.
No successor acknowledgment itemizes transferred files, decisions, unresolved issues, rollback state, or safe-decline conditions.
Predecessor availability is not proof that an independent operator could resume from an inspectable package.
Objective continuity is not person-to-person custody.

support_elements: extensive prior Cabinet, diplomatic, legal, and administrative experience
support_adjusted_surplus_adjudication.reason: The new records strengthen attribution and continuity but do not isolate output beyond the candidate's authority, staff, access, reputation, and institutional support.

next_action: Expose the seven-dimension vector to genuine external review; acquire an original HEW decision or recommendation object that links the welfare contradiction to a changed policy artifact; acquire a direct successor state-package receipt or attributable acknowledgment; obtain a resource-normalized comparator; and refuse CS-FT-01 until support adjustment, direct handoff, and completed independent review are established.
